A Change Data Capture pipeline for PostgreSQL
taps the Write-Ahead Log · delivers row-level events · ships with a R/W proxy
Postgres doesn't write your data to disk
It writes a 200-byte WAL record. That's enough.
the write-ahead contract · if the WAL record is on disk, the change is durable
// 03 of 16 · WAL is an append-only log
Every change flows through the WAL
16MB segment files in pg_wal/ · each record describes one byte-level change
one log · four use cases · one elegant design
pgoutput translates page bytes into structured rows
a replication slot is a cursor into this infinite, append-only event stream
A Go client speaks pgwire replication
forget to ack and WAL grows unbounded · ack matters
stream → filter → sink chain · 5 sinks · 4 decorators · 1 binary
each layer adds one concern · stack them however you want
// records latency, event counts, replication lag
nil → ack the LSN · err → don't ack, replay on restart
five sinks today · adding a sixth is ~80 lines of Go
NDJSON to stdout · pipe to jq
all sinks support at-least-once · consumers dedupe by tracking the LSN
Getting events is easy. Delivering them reliably is the engineering.
Two flush triggers · whichever fires first
one POST with 100 events is much cheaper than 100 individual POSTs
mutex-protected · timer goroutine + Deliver goroutine share the buffer
a transparent TCP proxy that splits reads from writes
misroute a read → primary = suboptimal · misroute a write → replica = fails clearly
Speaking pgwire at the byte level
raw TCP for clients · pgx pools for backends (handles SCRAM-SHA-256)
'I' idle · 'T' in-transaction · 'E' failed-transaction — the Z byte matters
SELECT · SHOW · EXPLAIN · SET · RESET · DISCARD
INSERT · UPDATE · DELETE · CREATE · ALTER · DROP · TRUNCATE · VACUUM
unknown → safe default (primary) · same heuristic as PgBouncer, ProxySQL, Vitess
I understood WAL conceptually before this project.
Between knowing about the wire protocol and
parsing 'Z' bytes off a TCP socket at 2 AM.
PostgreSQL CDC pipeline + read/write split proxy
written in Go · ~5,000 lines · 86% test coverage on proxy
